story.title: Serbia Holds Crucial Election as Student-Led Opposition Challenges Vucic's Rule
story.summary: Serbia is conducting a parliamentary election that could potentially end Aleksandar Vucic's long-standing leadership. The election follows nearly two years of protests led by students, which were ignited by a deadly railway station collapse. Early reports indicate a significant voter turnout, reflecting the public's engagement in this pivotal political moment.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in this election?
explore_lenses.title: A snap vote recast Vucic’s role
explore_lenses.summary: This is an early parliamentary election, not a presidential contest. Vučić dissolved the 2023-elected assembly, resigned the presidency in September, and is seeking to return as prime minister through his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).

claims.text: The Serbian government says Vučić dissolved the parliament elected in December 2023 and scheduled early parliamentary elections for October 25, 2026.
Vučić resigned the presidency in September to lead the SNS campaign; if SNS wins the most votes and can form a government, he would become prime minister.

The contest is unusually competitive because the student-backed list has consolidated a protest movement into an electoral challenger; AP reported the two leading camps were regarded as neck-and-neck before results.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after votes are cast?
explore_lenses.title: Results, challenges and government formation
explore_lenses.summary: Election-night projections are not the official result. The Republic Electoral Commission handles results and objections, while legal challenges can reach the Administrative Court; a new assembly then validates mandates before a government can be formed.

claims.text: AP reported that the state election commission was not expected to release its official tally before Monday, October 26, while Vučić said his camp would issue projections after polls closed.

Under Serbia’s parliamentary-election law, voters, candidates and list submitters can object to alleged electoral irregularities within 24 hours; the Republic Electoral Commission has 48 hours to decide, and appeals may then go to the Administrative Court.
If the Administrative Court annuls an electoral action or election, the law requires the relevant action or vote to be repeated within 10 days at the latest.
Forecast: ACLED analyst Magda Anastasijevic told AP that recent electoral violence could escalate, particularly if the outcome is disputed.

story_report.summary: Serbia voted in an early parliamentary election on Oct. 25 that tested Aleksandar Vučić’s political dominance against a student-backed opposition forged from protests after a deadly 2024 railway-station collapse. The contest was regarded as unusually close, and the immediate outcome was not yet clear: the official tally was not expected before Monday, while any eventual government will depend on seats and coalition negotiations.

sections.heading: Early Election Reshapes Vučić’s Role
sections.body: The Serbian government said Vučić dissolved the parliament elected in December 2023 and called the Oct. 25 early vote. He resigned the presidency in September to lead the Serbian Progressive Party, or SNS, campaign. If SNS wins the most votes and can assemble a governing majority, he would become prime minister.

sections.heading: Student Movement Tests Governing Party
sections.body: Student-led protests began after the deadly railway-station collapse in 2024 and were subsequently consolidated into an electoral list challenging SNS. AP reported before results that the two leading camps were viewed as neck-and-neck. An ACLED analyst told AP that recent electoral violence could escalate, particularly if the result is disputed; that assessment is a forecast rather than a confirmed outcome.

sections.heading: Results Face Legal Review Process
sections.body: The state election commission was not expected to issue its official tally before Oct. 26, although Vučić said his camp would release projections after polls closed. Serbian law allows voters, candidates and list submitters to object to alleged irregularities within 24 hours; the election commission has 48 hours to rule, with appeals available to the Administrative Court. If the court annuls an electoral action or election, the relevant process must be repeated within 10 days at the latest.

unresolved.text: The final vote count, seat allocation, any legal challenges and the coalition able to form a government remained unresolved as of Oct. 25, 2026.

related_stories.summary: The Justice Department has initiated a lawsuit aimed at blocking the certification of an upcoming election in Alaska. The lawsuit argues that the presence of two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot could lead to voter confusion. Legal experts are questioning the authority of the Justice Department in this matter.

related_stories.title: Obama and Trump Campaign Ahead of Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: As early voting for the midterm elections begins, both Barack Obama and Donald Trump are actively campaigning. Obama is urging voters to support Democratic candidates, emphasizing the importance of the election as a chance to counteract the current administration's policies. Meanwhile, Trump is rallying Republican support as both parties leverage their presidential influence during this critical period.
